DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

The Diary Beside the Declaration

STS-HS11-L3-1400P-HSELA1112-HJD-MNA-01 • HS English 11-12 • Foundational U.S. Documents: Themes, Purposes, and Rhetorical Features
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Historical journals let a reader stand inside a moment instead of reading about it. Layla, Tarek, and Rania are pairing invented diary entries from a family who arrived from Beirut and Casablanca with the exact lines those readers met for the first time in English. A diary says I felt. The Declaration says we hold.
Which one persuades a stranger more, and what does each one want from its reader?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Layla doing?
Look at the picture. Can you explain what Layla is doing and why she is doing it, in two connected sentences, and add what she is making a record of?
2
What is Tarek holding?
Look at the picture. Can you explain what Tarek has in his hands and why he is holding it up, in two connected sentences, and add why one family record is shown this large?
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Can you explain what the teacher is doing and why she is doing it, in two connected sentences, and add why an adult is welcoming people this way?
4
What room is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Can you explain what kind of room this is and how you can tell, in two connected sentences, and add why this kind of room was chosen for this work?
5
Tell me about the exhibit wall.
Look at the picture. Can you explain what is on the big wall and why it is up there, in two connected sentences, and add how the handwriting and the printed words speak to each other?
6
What is Rania wearing?
Look at the picture. Can you explain what Rania has on and why she might be wearing it, in two connected sentences, and add what her clothing adds to the picture of this family record?
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: CCSS.ELA-LITERACY.RI.11-12.9 — Analyze foundational U.S. documents for themes, purposes, and rhetorical features. ELD (Speaking — official ELPAC “Talk About a Scene”): PI.A.1, PII.B.3, PII.B.4, PII.B.5.
